exhibitScheduleEvidence: 'Form of Compliance Certificate' appears at char offset 2604 of the preamble, as a table-of-contents-style Exhibit-list entry (a mention of a document TYPE this Credit Agreement requires the Borrower to later deliver, per its own Section 5.02(?)/Article covenant, not a claim about what THIS document is).
classifierMatchingOrderExact: Re-executed lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/document-classifier.ts's own RULES array (13 entries) against the identical 3000-char preamble slice, in the EXACT array order the production `for (const rule of RULES)` loop uses: COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE (array index 7) is tested BEFORE CREDIT_AGREEMENT (array index 12). COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE's pattern /\bcompliance certificate\b/i matches at char 2604; CREDIT_AGREEMENT's pattern /\bcredit agreement\b/i would have matched at char 276 - textually 2328 characters EARLIER - but is never reached because the loop returns on the FIRST rule (by array order) that matches anywhere in the whole 3000-char window, not the rule whose evidence appears earliest IN THE TEXT.
winningClassificationSignal: COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE, evidence 'Compliance Certificate' at char 2604 (via Tier 2's broad preamble scan, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_TITLE_PATTERN, confidence 0.9).
competingCreditAgreementSignal: CREDIT_AGREEMENT, evidence 'CREDIT AGREEMENT' at char 276 - the document's own real caption, textually the FIRST classification-relevant string in the entire document, but never reached by the Tier 2 loop because it is checked later in RULES array order.
exactProductionFunctions: classifyDocument (lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/document-classifier.ts:96) - Tier 2's `for (const rule of RULES) { const evidence = findEvidence(rule.patterns, preamble); if (evidence) return ...; }` loop
findEvidence (document-classifier.ts:78) - scans the WHOLE preamble string per rule with no positional comparison across rules
whyComplianceCertificateWins: Tier 1 (self-referential title, SELF_REFERENCE_RE = `(this "X")`) does not fire for doc-a - doc-a's caption uses the plain, un-self-referential financing-document convention ('CREDIT AGREEMENT ... Dated as of ... Between ... as Borrower ...'), not the '(this "Credit Agreement")' phrasing Tier 1 was built to catch (that phrasing is itself more common in amendments than in a fresh base agreement). Falling through to Tier 2, the ONLY signal the loop uses to pick a winner among multiple rules that each match somewhere in the 3000-char window is RULE-ARRAY POSITION, never text position and never any notion of 'is this evidence describing the document itself vs. something the document merely mentions/requires/attaches.' COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE happens to sit earlier in the RULES array than CREDIT_AGREEMENT (an incidental consequence of how the array was originally ordered for a different reason - AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT/SUPPLEMENTAL_INDENTURE/etc. needing to precede their more generic parent types per this file's own header comment), so it wins regardless of its later, weaker, TOC/exhibit-list textual context.

rootCauseClassification.primary: A. first-match ordering (RULES array order, not text position, decides the winner among multiple textually-present signals)
rootCauseClassification.contributing: B. unscoped whole-document(-window) keyword matching (findEvidence scans the full 3000-char preamble with no distinction between the document's own caption and a later table-of-contents/exhibit-list mention)

notTheCause.C_tocContaminationAlone: Related but not sufficient alone - the TOC entry is real evidence of SOMETHING, the defect is that it is never down-weighted relative to the earlier, stronger caption evidence.
notTheCause.D_exhibitTitleContaminationAlone: Same as C - a contributing factor, not the root mechanism.
notTheCause.E_headingRankContamination: Not applicable - document-classifier.ts does not use structural heading rank/hierarchy at all; it operates on raw preamble text only.
notTheCause.F_titleZoneWeightingFailure: This IS a secondary framing of the same root cause: the classifier has no title-zone concept at all (unlike document-identity.ts, which already extracts a bounded, position-first title match). The classifier's Tier 2 never consults document-identity.ts's own title extraction.
